mode.plaintext: Not encrypted — the agent connects over plain HTTP

edit.title: Edit Environment
edit.description: Change the name and connection details for this environment.
edit.setDefaultHint: New sessions open on this environment.
edit.activeHint: Inactive environments are kept but not polled.

create.title: Add Environment
create.name: Name
create.agentDescription: A lightweight agent binary runs on the remote machine and connects outbound to McHarbor via WebSocket. No ports need to be opened on the remote host. After creating the environment, you'll receive a token to configure the agent.
create.hostKeyFingerprintHelp: Verify the remote server fingerprint before deploying. Example: ssh-keyscan <host> | ssh-keygen -lf - -E sha256
create.sshPasswordWarning: Password authentication is less secure than key-based authentication. Consider using an SSH key instead.
create.useExistingTokenDescription: Paste the token already issued by another McHarbor host that this agent connects back to. Leave unchecked to generate a fresh token.
create.existingTokenHelp: Find the token under → Identity & access on the originating host. Format: agt_ followed by 64 hex characters.
create.caCertHelp: Required when the API server uses a self-signed certificate. Leave empty if its certificate is publicly trusted.
create.saveCredentialsHelp: The host, user and method are stored on the environment. The key or password goes into the secrets vault, and McHarbor keeps only a reference to it — so updating the agent later is one click and no re-typing.

hostChecks.title: Host checks
hostChecks.body: Ask this host what it already has, before the agent goes on it.
hostChecks.hint: Fill in the SSH host, user and host key fingerprint first.
hostChecks.dockerReady: Docker is installed on this host.
hostChecks.dockerNotReady: Docker is not installed on this host.
hostChecks.vmReady: This host is ready to run virtual machines.
hostChecks.vmNotReady: This host cannot run virtual machines yet.
hostChecks.vmNote: Virtual machines also need the agent installed as a binary under systemd. A containerised agent cannot host them.

prereq.title: Prerequisites
prereq.body: Check what this host already has before deploying.
prereq.notChecked: Not checked yet. Fill in the SSH details and check.
prereq.ready: Ready to continue. Nothing required is missing.
prereq.blockedMissing: Something this deploy method needs is missing. Tick it for install, or install it by hand and check again.
prereq.blockedEscalation: The ticked packages cannot be installed: this host offers no way to run privileged commands. Enter the root password or fix sudo.
prereq.noRemediation: No install command is known for this distribution. Install it by hand.
prereq.installBody: Only what you tick is installed, and only on this host. Nothing is installed unless you ask.
prereq.escalationNote: Runs over SSH using the escalation detected above.
prereq.rootPasswordHelp: This host has no sudo, so installing uses su. The password is used for this run only and is never stored.

escalation.label: Privileged commands run:
escalation.sudo_password: through sudo, with the SSH password
escalation.su: through su, with the root password
escalation.unavailable: not at all — no root, no sudo, no root password

detail.notFoundDescription: The requested environment could not be found.

agentLog.title: Agent Log
agentLog.description: Lines the agent recorded while it could not reach McHarbor, replayed after it reconnected.
agentLog.emptyDescription: The agent has not been offline since it last connected, or nothing has been replayed yet.

detail.title: Environment Details

activity.title: Activity Settings
activity.description: Control live event tracking, container metrics, change highlights, and Docker disk usage alerts for this environment.
activity.trackContainerEventsDescription: Track container events (start, stop, restart, and similar actions) from this environment in real-time.
activity.collectContainerMetricsTitle: Collect CPU and memory usage statistics
activity.collectContainerMetricsDescription: Poll this environment for live container CPU and memory statistics used by dashboards and list views.
activity.highlightContainerChangesTitle: Show amber glow when container values change
activity.highlightContainerChangesDescription: Highlight containers in the containers list when their state or live values change.
activity.diskUsageNotificationsTitle: Send notifications when Docker disk usage exceeds the threshold
activity.diskUsageNotificationsDescription: Send an in-app notification when Docker storage crosses the configured threshold for this environment.
activity.diskCapacityNote: Threshold alerts use the Docker storage driver capacity reported by the engine when it is available.
activity.diskUsageExceededDescription: Docker storage is at {{percent}}% of capacity (threshold: {{threshold}}%, current usage: {{total}}).

automation.title: Automation Settings
automation.description: Environment-level defaults for scheduled update checks, image pruning, and timezone handling.
automation.scheduledUpdateCheckDescription: Periodically check all containers in this environment for available image updates.
automation.scheduledUpdateCheckHint: Automatically check for container updates on a schedule
automation.automaticImagePruningDescription: Automatically remove unused Docker images every day at 03:00 in this environment's timezone to free up disk space.
automation.automaticImagePruningHint: Runs daily at 03:00 using the timezone below
automation.imagePruneDanglingOnlyDescription: When enabled, only dangling (untagged) images are removed. Disable to also remove any unused tagged images.
automation.timezoneDescription: Used for scheduling auto-updates, git syncs, and image pruning.

retention.title: Retention & Pruning
retention.description: Configure log retention, automatic container pruning, the auto-update maintenance window, and metric retention for this environment.
retention.logRetentionDescription: How long container log history is retained before being pruned.
retention.logRetentionHint: Set to 0 to keep logs forever. Range: 0 to 3650 days.
retention.containerPruneDescription: Automatically remove stopped containers that have been stopped for the configured number of days.
retention.autoUpdateDescription: Restrict automatic container image updates to a specific time window and days of the week.
retention.metricRetentionDescription: How long collected container and host metrics are retained before being pruned.
retention.metricRetentionHint: Set to 0 to keep metrics forever. Range: 0 to 8760 hours (1 year).

host.title: Host
host.agentLimitedNotice: This environment is connected through a remote agent. Live host metrics and prune actions are not available; only Docker-level stats are shown.

hostFs.title: Host filesystem
hostFs.unavailable: Host filesystem usage is not available for this environment.

prune.title: Prune
prune.description: Free disk space by removing unused Docker resources. Destructive — confirm each action.
prune.agentLimited: Prune is not available for agent environments: the Docker daemon on the remote host is not directly accessible.

system.label: System (containers, images, networks)
system.title: Prune system
system.description: Remove all stopped containers, unused images, and unused networks. Named volumes are not touched.
system.withVolumesDescription: Remove stopped containers, unused images, unused networks, AND unused named volumes. Data in named volumes not used by any container will be permanently deleted.

volumes.label: Volumes (destructive)
volumes.title: Prune volumes
volumes.description: Remove all unused named volumes. Data in unused named volumes will be permanently deleted.

images.label: Images
images.title: Prune images
images.description: Remove all dangling and unused images.

docker.title: Docker engine
docker.description: Detailed information about the Docker daemon running in this environment.
docker.unavailable: Docker engine information is unavailable for this environment.

processes.title: Container processes
processes.description: Live resource usage (CPU, memory, network, block I/O) for running containers in this environment.

hostTerminal.title: Host terminal
hostTerminal.description: Interactive shell on the remote host running through the agent (or via privileged container for local envs).
hostTerminal.warning: This session has full host-level access. Run commands only when you understand the impact.
hostTerminal.connectError: Could not connect to the host terminal.

access.title: SSH access
access.description: How McHarbor reaches this host to install or update the agent. The credential itself lives in the secrets vault and is never shown here.
access.notConfigured: No SSH access has been saved for this environment yet.
access.fingerprintHelp: The SHA256 fingerprint McHarbor pins when connecting. Leave as saved unless the host key changed.
access.secretHelp: Pick a secret already in the vault, or enter a new key or password below to file one.
access.credentialHelp: A key or password entered here is written to the secrets vault and never returned to the browser again. Leave both blank to keep the stored credential.

hostUpdates.unavailable: The host operating system could not be read, so nothing here can be changed.
hostUpdates.title: Host OS updates
hostUpdates.checkFailed: The update check did not complete.
hostUpdates.osFailed: The host operating system could not be read.
hostUpdates.upToDate: The host has no pending package updates.
hostUpdates.scheduleDescription: McHarbor checks for pending host packages on this schedule. It never installs them on its own.
hostUpdates.newPackagesDescription: Lets an upgrade pull in packages it does not already have. Without this, a kernel update is reported as “kept back” and never applies, because a new kernel ABI needs new image and header packages. Nothing is ever removed.
hostUpdates.skipUnavailableDescription: Carries on when a mirror no longer serves a package, instead of failing the whole upgrade. apt uses --fix-missing, dnf uses --skip-broken with skip_if_unavailable, and yum uses --skip-broken. zypper, apk and pacman have no safe equivalent and ignore it.
hostUpdates.removeUnusedDescription: After a successful upgrade, removes packages that were installed as dependencies and are no longer needed, including old kernels on Debian and Ubuntu. apt, dnf and yum use autoremove, pacman removes orphans; apk and zypper have no safe equivalent, so the option is ignored there.
hostUpdates.refreshNote: The package lists are always refreshed before an upgrade, and a failed download is retried once after a fresh refresh.
hostUpdates.recoveryUnsupported: This environment's agent predates Skip unavailable packages and the automatic retry, and ignores both. Update the agent from Settings → Updates.
hostUpdates.applyDescription_one: Installs {{count}} pending package update on this host. The output streams into the page.
hostUpdates.applyDescription_other: Installs {{count}} pending package updates on this host. The output streams into the page.
hostUpdates.applyDefaultsNote: These start from the environment's saved defaults on the Automatic check card, and apply to this run only.
hostUpdates.hintSkipUnavailable: Some packages could not be downloaded, even after the package lists were refreshed and the upgrade retried once. Turn on Skip unavailable packages and run the update again to install everything else.

hostReboot.title: Reboot
hostReboot.requiredDescription: The host reports that a reboot is required to finish installing updates.
hostReboot.idleDescription: The last reboot McHarbor ran on this host.
hostReboot.demoBlocked: Demo mode never reboots a host.

phase.guests: Shutting down virtual machines and LXC containers
phase.reboot: Waiting for the host to come back

reason.demo_mode: Demo mode never reboots a host.
reason.reboot_in_progress: A reboot of this host is already in progress.
reason.invalid_time: Choose a date and time in the future, at most 90 days ahead.
reason.not_scheduled: There is no scheduled reboot to cancel.
reason.host_unreachable: The host could not be reached, so nothing was stopped.
reason.kubernetes_node: This host is a Kubernetes node that was not confirmed as drained, so nothing was stopped.
reason.swarm_worker: This host is a Swarm worker running service tasks that was not confirmed as drained, so nothing was stopped.
reason.swarm_pause_failed: The Swarm node could not be paused, so nothing was stopped.
reason.guest_not_graceful: A virtual machine or LXC container cannot be shut down gracefully, so nothing was stopped.
reason.guest_shutdown_failed: A virtual machine or LXC container refused the shutdown request. The reboot was cancelled.
reason.guest_timeout: A virtual machine or LXC container did not shut down in time. It was left running and the reboot was cancelled.
reason.container_stop_failed: A Docker container could not be sent its stop signal. The reboot was cancelled.
reason.container_timeout: A Docker container did not stop in time. It was left running and the reboot was cancelled.
reason.reboot_command_failed: The host refused the reboot command. The containers McHarbor stopped were started again.
reason.host_not_back: The host has not come back after the reboot.
reason.host_did_not_restart: The host is reachable but did not restart.
reason.interrupted: McHarbor stopped while the reboot was stopping workloads, so the host was not rebooted.
reason.restore_partial: The host rebooted, but not everything could be started again.

dialog.title: Reboot this machine?
dialog.description: McHarbor stops everything on the host gracefully, then asks systemd to reboot. Nothing is killed: if a workload does not stop in time, the reboot is refused and the host keeps running.
dialog.dateTimeHint: In your browser's time zone. McHarbor runs the reboot once, at this moment.
dialog.detecting: Detecting what runs on this host…
dialog.drainedLabel: I have cordoned and drained this node
dialog.drainedDescription: Required for a Kubernetes node or a Swarm worker: McHarbor cannot move those workloads for you and refuses the reboot without this confirmation.

disclaimer.containers: Each container receives its own stop signal (SIGTERM unless configured otherwise) and gets up to 10 minutes to exit. None is killed. Containers with the restart policy always or unless-stopped are started again once the host is back.
disclaimer.containersDetected: Detected on this host: {{total}} running, {{returning}} started again afterwards.
disclaimer.vms: Each VM gets an ACPI shutdown request and up to 10 minutes to power off. There is no forced power-off. A VM starts again after the reboot only if autostart is on.
disclaimer.lxc: Each container is sent its init system's halt signal and waited for the same way, never killed. It starts again after the reboot only if autostart is on.
disclaimer.guestsDetected: Detected on this host: {{guests}} guests running (virtual machines and system containers).
disclaimer.guestBlockers: These cannot be shut down gracefully and block the reboot: {{names}}
disclaimer.kubernetes: McHarbor does not cordon or drain Kubernetes nodes. Drain the node first (kubectl drain), otherwise the kubelet stops its pods during shutdown.
disclaimer.kubernetesDetected: Kubernetes detected on this host ({{names}}). Confirm below that the node is drained.
disclaimer.swarm: A manager node is paused so its service tasks move to other nodes as they stop, and set back to active after the reboot. A worker cannot pause itself: drain it from a manager first.
disclaimer.swarmManager: This host is a Swarm manager and is paused during the reboot.
disclaimer.swarmWorker: This host is a Swarm worker running {{tasks}} service tasks. Drain it from a manager and confirm below.
disclaimer.mcharbor: McHarbor itself runs on this machine and is offline until the machine is back. The reboot is finished, and stopped containers are started again, when McHarbor starts up.
disclaimer.unknown: Could not be detected on this host.
disclaimer.refused: If anything does not stop in time, McHarbor refuses the reboot instead of forcing it, starts the Docker containers it stopped again, and shows the reason on this card.

hostLogs.title: Host logs
hostLogs.description: Bounded snapshots of system, kernel, authentication, and Docker daemon logs from the host running this environment.
hostLogs.unavailable: Host logs are unavailable for this environment.
hostLogs.availableFilesLabel: Log files found on this host
hostLogs.fallbackNote: None of the expected log files were present, so the largest log on this host was read instead: {{file}}

notices.permission_denied: A host log file exists but McHarbor does not have permission to read it. A fallback source was tried.
notices.no_supported_log_source: No readable file log or supported journal source was found for this host.
notices.no_var_log_dir: The host has no /var/log directory, so no file-based logs could be read.
notices.no_journalctl: journalctl is not installed on this host, so journal logs could not be read.
notices.journalctl_failed: journalctl returned an error. Any output shown below may be incomplete.

hostLogPreview.title: Recent log lines
hostLogPreview.description: Last few lines from this host's system, kernel, authentication, or Docker daemon log. Open the Logs tab for the full view.
hostLogPreview.empty: No log lines available on the host. Try a different source or check the host's log directory.

agentHealth.title: Agent health
agentHealth.summaryNoSamples: No samples recorded yet. The strip fills in as McHarbor observes the agent's keepalive.
agentHealth.summaryNeverConnected: This agent has never connected, so there is nothing to judge yet. Install it on the remote host and it will dial in on its own.
agentHealth.summaryDisconnected: The agent is not connected. It was last seen at {{time}}; until it dials back in, nothing on this environment can be managed.
agentHealth.summaryDegraded: {{degraded}} of the last {{total}} samples were degraded — the agent answered its keepalive late or not at all. The ping runs every {{interval}} s.
agentHealth.summaryHealthy: The agent answered all {{total}} recorded keepalives. The ping runs every {{interval}} s and the last round trip took {{latency}} ms.
agentHealth.stripLabel: Agent health history: {{total}} samples, {{degraded}} degraded, {{down}} disconnected

agentUptime.title: Agent uptime
agentUptime.summaryNoSamples: No samples recorded yet. The strip fills in as McHarbor observes the agent.
agentUptime.summaryAllUp: The agent was connected for all {{total}} recorded samples.
agentUptime.summaryWithDowntime: The agent was disconnected for {{down}} of the last {{total}} samples — {{percent}}% up, across {{outages}} outages.
agentUptime.stripLabel: Agent uptime history: {{total}} samples, {{up}} connected, {{down}} disconnected

mode.push: Pushed by the agent every {{seconds}} s
mode.pull: Pulled one container at a time
mode.direct: Read directly from the Docker connection

reason.agent_too_old: Agent {{version}} (build {{build}}) cannot push stats. Build {{requiredBuild}} of {{requiredVersion}} or newer can.
reason.awaiting_first_batch: The agent was asked to push and its first batch has not arrived yet.
reason.agent_metrics_disabled: Agent metrics are turned off in Settings → System → Agent.

detail.updateAgentHelp: Re-runs the saved SSH deployment to install the current agent. Needs deployment details to have been remembered.

agentToken.title: Agent Token Created
agentToken.description: Save this token now — it will not be shown again.
agentToken.installInfoDescription: Use these commands to install or reinstall the agent on the remote host. The token is sensitive.
agentToken.binaryIntro: A native install — the binary under systemd. It is the only install that can host virtual machines or system containers.
agentToken.binaryDownloadNote: Takes the agent this McHarbor was built with, so the two versions match.
agentToken.binaryForegroundNote: Runs in the foreground, for a quick check. It does not survive a reboot — install the service below for a permanent agent.
agentToken.runAsService: Install as a systemd service (run as root)
agentToken.serviceNote: The token is written into the unit file, which is why the file is kept root-readable only. Follow the start with journalctl -u mcharbor-agent -f.
agentToken.serviceOtherPlatforms: No systemd on this host? Wire the binary into whatever init it uses. McHarbor ships no service installer for Windows or macOS.
agentToken.installUrlNote: Run on the remote host. Forces the container install and fails if Docker is not usable there.
agentToken.scriptExpiry: This URL expires after 24 hours and can only be used once.
agentToken.wssHint: Connection uses wss:// — make sure the remote host trusts the McHarbor certificate.
agentToken.transferHttpsHint: File transfers are pushed to https://<agent-host>:8788 — the agent must trust the McHarbor certificate.
agentToken.composeNote: Save as docker-compose.yml on the remote host and run docker compose up -d.
agentToken.composeLoadNote: Run the first two lines of the Docker command first, to load the agent image from McHarbor. Then save this as docker-compose.yml on the remote host and run docker compose up -d.
agentToken.insecureTlsHint: On by default because a stock McHarbor signs its own. The agent is then pinned to this server's certificate authority with MCHARBOR_PIN, so it trusts that one CA and nothing else. Turn it off when yours is signed by a CA the remote host already trusts.

confirm.removeDescription: This will remove this environment from McHarbor.

migrate.title: Migrate connection
migrate.description: Change how McHarbor reaches this host. The environment keeps its id, so its stacks, metrics, activity and compute resources come with it.
migrate.existingTokenHint: Leave empty to have McHarbor issue a new token. Paste one only when the agent is already deployed and holds it.
migrate.immediateHint: The environment switches now and stops working until the agent connects.
migrate.gracefulHint: The environment keeps using its current connection until the agent connects with the new token.
migrate.revokeWarning: The current agent token is revoked and the connected agent is disconnected. It cannot reconnect unless you migrate back and issue a new token.
migrate.pendingNotice: Waiting for an agent to connect. This environment switches to {{target}} the moment it does, and keeps working until then.
migrate.deployAgentHint: McHarbor deploys the agent container on this host through the connection it already has, and the environment switches over on its own once it connects.
migrate.deployAgentOffHint: You get a token and install the agent yourself. The environment keeps working until it connects.
migrate.insecureTlsHint: On by default because a stock McHarbor signs its own certificate. Turn it off if yours is signed by a CA the host trusts.
migrate.deployFailed: The agent could not be installed
migrate.deployFailedHint: Nothing was changed — the environment is back on its previous connection and the token has been revoked.
migrate.pendingFailsafe: If it has not connected within 15 minutes McHarbor puts this environment back the way it was, removes the agent it deployed, and revokes the token.

merge.title: Merge environments
merge.description: Fold another environment into {{target}} and delete it.
merge.sourceHint: Everything attached to it is re-pointed at this environment, and the row is then deleted.
merge.warning: This cannot be undone. Rows the kept environment already has an equivalent of — a pool of the same name, the same settings row — are discarded rather than duplicated.
merge.planEmpty: Nothing is attached to that environment.
merge.defaultMoved: The default-environment flag moves with it.

duplicates.title: Another environment reaches this same machine ({{hostname}})
duplicates.body: Both this environment and {{others}} report the same Docker daemon. Two environments on one host double its polling cost and count it twice in reporting.

hostServices.title: Services
hostServices.empty: No services reported by this host
hostServices.truncated: The host reported more services than McHarbor shows at once; the list is cut short.

protected.agent: Protected: this is the McHarbor agent itself. It can be restarted, not stopped or disabled.
protected.ssh: Protected: stopping SSH could lock you out of the host.
protected.dbus: Protected: the system message bus that systemd and most services depend on.
protected.runtime: Protected: the container runtime the McHarbor agent drives.
protected.mcharbor: Protected: this runs McHarbor itself. It can be restarted, not stopped or disabled.
protected.self_runtime: Protected: the container runtime McHarbor itself runs on. It can be restarted, not stopped or disabled.

toast.agentRestarting: The agent is restarting; it will reconnect in a few seconds
toast.mcharborRestarting: {{unit}} is restarting; McHarbor is unavailable until it is back

stop.title: Stop {{unit}}?
stop.description: The service stops now. It starts again at the next boot if it is enabled.

restart.title: Restart {{unit}}?
restart.description: The service stops and starts again. Anything connected to it is interrupted.

disable.title: Disable {{unit}}?
disable.description: The service no longer starts at boot. Whether it is running now does not change.

revert.title: Revert {{unit}} to its vendor configuration?
revert.description: The McHarbor override is deleted and systemd is reloaded. Its content cannot be recovered.

reload.title: Reload systemd?
reload.description: Runs systemctl daemon-reload: systemd rereads every unit file and drop-in. Running services are not restarted.

confirm.agentRestartWarning: This is the McHarbor agent. Restarting it drops the connection to this host until the agent reconnects, usually within a few seconds.
confirm.mcharborRestartWarning: Restarting {{unit}} takes McHarbor down with it. This page stops responding until McHarbor is back, usually within a minute.

override.title: Configuration of {{unit}}
override.description: Changes go into a drop-in override, as systemctl edit does. The vendor unit file is never modified.
override.loadFailed: The unit's configuration could not be read
override.notYetCreated: No override exists yet; saving creates it.

not_agent.title: Services need an agent
not_agent.description: Only a host with a McHarbor agent installed natively can have its services managed.

not_native.title: Services need a native agent
not_native.description: This agent runs in a container, which cannot reach the host's systemd. Install the agent as a binary under systemd to manage services.

offline.title: The agent is not connected
offline.description: Services can be managed again as soon as the agent reconnects.

agent_outdated.title: Update the agent to use Services
agent_outdated.description: This agent is {{version}} build {{build}}. Services need {{minVersion}} build {{minBuild}} or newer. Update it from Settings → Updates → Agents.

no_systemd.title: This host does not run systemd
no_systemd.description: The agent found no systemd on this host, so there are no services to manage.

self_unreachable.title: McHarbor cannot reach the machine it is installed on

self_no_systemd.title: This machine does not run systemd
self_no_systemd.description: The machine McHarbor is installed on does not run systemd, so there are no services to manage.
